unit.title: Retry-Safe Key/Value Operations: Contract, Traces, and Evidence
unit.learner_profile: Strong in algorithms; deliberately practicing software contracts, failure modeling, deterministic testing, observability, and evidence-based debugging.
learning_outcomes: Turn an informal distributed-service goal into an explicit failure model and client-visible contract.
Specify retry-safe state transitions for lost, duplicated, delayed, and reordered messages.
Derive deterministic trace tests and observability from named safety invariants.
Keep claims within the modeled crash, persistence, concurrency, and material boundaries.
Record hypotheses, counterexamples, revisions, and reproducible evidence.
included: A self-contained fictional key/value service scenario
Deterministic event-trace analysis and test planning
A bounded debugging record and production-gap review
excluded: Official MIT lectures, papers, labs, assignment specifications, starter code, and tests
Raft, replication, leader election, log agreement, membership change, and sharding
A claim of official credit or whole-course completion

required_evidence: All three learner outputs are present and internally consistent.
The submission contains checkable contracts, traces, test oracles, and bounded claims.
The debugging log records reproducible hypothesis-experiment-observation-revision cycles.
An independent examiner evaluates the preserved learner outputs against examiner_only/RUBRIC.md.
The worker harness validates the examiner's structured result.
